title: Assessing Glacier Area Dynamics from 2000 to 2025 Using Multisensor Satellite Imagery
content: Glacier area changes in the upper Karatal catchment of the Dzungarian Alatau, Kazakhstan, were assessed for 2000–2025 using Landsat 5/7/8/9 and Sentinel-2 observations processed in Google Earth Engine. Mapping applied a Normalized Difference Snow Index threshold of 0.4 within glacier outlines provided by the Randolph Glacier Inventory version 7.0. Annual area estimates were available for 22 of the 26 calendar years; suitable observations were lacking for 2003–2005 and 2012. The anomalous estimate for 2009 was excluded from the trend analysis. Linear regression based on the remaining 21 annual estimates produced a slope of −0.92 km² per year, equivalent to 0.39% of the inventory reference area (234.9 km²) annually. However, the trend was not statistically significant (R² = 0.09; p = 0.18). Mean mapped glacier area was 219.4 km² in 2000–2004 and 187.9 km² in 2020–2025, a difference of 31.5 km² (14.4%). The 2000 estimate was 3.7% below the inventory baseline; since the same inventory provided the classification mask, the comparison evaluates internal consistency rather than independent accuracy. Considerable interannual variability (coefficient of variation: 12.0%) underscores uncertainties associated with observation conditions and multisensor data.
